B33.value: C17: 1 = estimate h₁ from target y⁺ and correlation, 2 = correct h₁ using y⁺ achieved in CFD.

B35.value: Correlations assume a smooth flat plate, turbulent flow and zero pressure gradient.

B41.value: L is the streamwise location along the surface or a chosen reference length. For a foil, it may be the chord.

B42.value: For a curved foil with a pressure gradient, δ₉₉ and h₁ are initial estimates. Check y⁺ after running CFD.

B43.value: Choose target y⁺ to suit the turbulence model and wall treatment. The default y⁺ = 1 is an example.

B44.value: In correction mode, use y⁺ and h₁ from the same wall region. The correction assumes approximately unchanged u_τ.

B45.value: Geometric progression: h_i = h₁·r^(i−1), T = h₁·(r^N−1)/(r−1). For r = 1: T = N·h₁.

B46.value: Automatic r solves T = target using 60 bisection steps. No Solver add-in or Excel iterative calculation is needed.

B47.value: FM101 calls r the maximum growth ratio. Here r matches T to the target; for fixed N it is the target coverage threshold.

B48.value: Method: Fluid Mechanics 101, Calculators & Tools, section 2, pp. 4–7. Accessed: 28 October 2026.

I27.value: No wall-treatment selection can be inferred from y+ alone. Check the STAR physics continuum.

B30.value: Local LE/TE targets are recommendations, not 50-case sweep variables. Use separate surface controls rather than trying to resolve the whole domain at the LE size.

B31.value: STAR may specify sizes as percentages of Base Size. Use absolute controls or carefully parameterized expressions; do not paste these numbers into percent fields.

B32.value: Cell count proxies are crude. A fully 3D VOF band across an 11.9 m span may dominate memory and disk requirements.

B33.value: For accuracy, shortlist meshes and perform 3+ level grid and time-step sensitivity on CL/CD and wave elevation.

A2.value: Flat free surface: H=0. Local CFL estimates depend on velocity component and local cell orientation; verify using STAR reports.

I6.value: use only in the wave refinement volume

I20.value: verify in actual STAR VOF solver

B23.value: Do not use freestream velocity divided by first prism height for normal CFL. Resolve VOF convection with flow-direction velocities and interface cell spacing.

B24.value: For wave-added resistance: spatial, temporal and wave-far-field convergence required. Implicit STAR solvers do not have a universal CFL < 1 requirement.

A1.value: MESH RESULTS | STAR OUTPUT RECEIVED HERE

A2.value: Measured columns B:I are intentionally blank. Macro outputs CSV with actual cell count and quality metrics only if report names are configured.

B14.value: Save a COPY of current .sim as baseline_mesh_only.sim. Stop the ongoing CFD solve before editing its mesh.

B15.value: Create the 5 scalar global parameters above with Length dimension and units m.

B16.value: Link them to the actual mesh controls, using absolute settings or well-defined expressions if STAR shows % of Base Size.

B17.value: Keep FIRST prism cell, prism TOTAL thickness, prism N and growth ratio fixed across all 50 grids: target Godø y+55.

B18.value: Create 4 Reports over the fluid volume: Batch_CellCount, Batch_MinVolumeChange, Batch_MinCellQuality and Batch_MaxSkewness.

B19.value: Put MeshSweep50.java and mesh_sweep_50.csv in the working folder beside the copied .sim.

B20.value: Smoke test first 3 cases (the Java file has CASE_LIMIT=3). Verify cell count changes and reports are nonempty.

B21.value: Only after that, set CASE_LIMIT=50 in Java and relaunch on the copied .sim. Macro DOES NOT run the CFD solver.

B22.value: Macro appends metric rows to mesh_results.csv and does not save 50 huge .sim files by default.

B23.value: Paste CSV data into Mesh Results after processing and shortlist 3+ meshes for controlled CFD convergence.

B27.value: 50 generated meshes may take longer and consume more RAM than one CFD run. Start with 3 cases, inspect timings, and avoid high-cost VOF grids.

B28.value: Missing reports produce blank numbers, not a PASS. The macro cannot identify prism coverage automatically without a case-specific report.

B29.value: The macro overwrites the ACTIVE mesh state in the working .sim, never run it on your only model copy or while the solver is working.

B30.value: Exact STAR-CCM+ menu paths and Java API can vary by version. Use Tools > Macro > Record in your installation to confirm parameter wiring.

B32.value: EXPORT: If you change any input or factor, export the Macro CSV tab alone as UTF-8 CSV and name it mesh_sweep_50.csv. The standalone CSV supplied here matches the shipped defaults.
